classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied general coordinate diagram to derive two midpoint coordinates, connect equal heights to parallelism and compare their horizontal separation with the base.

content.prompt: Use coordinate geometry to prove that the line joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half its length. Take the base of the triangle to be on the $x$-axis with one vertex at the origin.

spec.description: Triangle ABC on arrowed coordinate axes, with A at the origin, C on the positive x-axis and B above the axis between A and C horizontally. AC coincides with the x-axis. No midpoints are supplied. Ordinary source blue sides and red vertex markers are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: A=(0,0), B=(u,v), C=(c,0). The displayed representative triangle has c>0 and v>0; the horizontal position of B does not affect the proof.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied vertices, coordinate labels and axes are visible; midpoint labels and the joining segment are absent.

answer.short:
Let $M$ and $N$ be the midpoints of $AB$ and $BC$. Then $M=(\frac u2,\frac v2)$ and $N=(\frac{u+c}{2},\frac v2)$, so $MN\parallel AC$ and $MN=\frac c2=\frac12 AC$.

Use the midpoint formula, compare gradients, then subtract the horizontal coordinates.
answer.worked:
Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$ and $N$ the midpoint of $BC$. By the midpoint formula:
$$\begin{align*}M&=\left(\frac{0+u}{2},\frac{0+v}{2}\right)\\M&=\left(\frac u2,\frac v2\right),\\N&=\left(\frac{u+c}{2},\frac{v+0}{2}\right)\\N&=\left(\frac{u+c}{2},\frac v2\right).\end{align*}$$
Their gradients are:
$$\begin{align*}m_{MN}&=\frac{\frac v2-\frac v2}{\frac{u+c}{2}-\frac u2}\\m_{MN}&=0,\\m_{AC}&=\frac{0-0}{c-0}\\m_{AC}&=0.\end{align*}$$
The equal gradients show that $MN\parallel AC$. Since both intervals are horizontal and $c>0$ in the chosen diagram:
$$\begin{align*}MN&=\frac{u+c}{2}-\frac u2\\MN&=\frac c2,\\AC&=c,\\MN&=\frac12 AC.\end{align*}$$
Thus the line joining the midpoints is parallel to the third side and half its length. Any chosen third side can be placed on the $x$-axis in this way.
